metadata.Title: calm dance by OK
metadata.Description: Nikon D750. ICM. This road, this town, this heartbeat. There's no going back to the now. I leave this town. Taking only nameless emotions with me. My chest fills with pain and anticipation, and I can't tell which is forward and which is backward. For just a moment, the past and future pass each other by. That trembling carries me to the next town. This is not a memory. It is the light of an emotion that exists only here and now.

metadata.Title: clump by OK feat.tsitraton
metadata.Description: tsitraton draws lines before they have meaning. I too sometimes draw patterns before they have meaning, or patterns that have lost their meaning. This painting has no meaning, but there is white space where anyone who wants meaning can freely attach it. These lines are rhythm. A rhythm that has developed over time for tsitraton and okayaman. Some people find it pleasant, others find it unpleasant. That's fine. That's what's good. This is my personal interpretation, but these two line artists stopped the lines just before meaning began to emerge. This resulting work is meaningless, but I named it "clump". It is both plant-like and conceptual. That's what I thought. --- At first, this work was contained within tsitraton's lines. Something was missing. When I went beyond the boundaries, this was the result. Traces of growth over time.

metadata.Title: OOPARTS #30 being there
metadata.Description: Wherever we exist, it's the same. We exist together. We enjoy both convenience and inconvenience. A place where we can touch the earth. A texture like a historical Japanese painting. It was a memorable day in March. A quote from my own palette. The block height of 938730 at the start of March 1st. This also marks the beginning of my new life on Bitcoin time. The beauty of negative space. That's a space for you to enter.

metadata.Title: OOPARTS #29 quiet moment
metadata.Description: photo / Nikon D750 / - Compressing the quiet everyday. Lowering the resolution of reality allows the unreality to seep in. - / This work intentionally degrades the most basic "device for the act of seeing"—a window—found in the quiet of everyday life, through excessive compression. As a result, the landscape is reduced to unrealistic particles, and the "continuity" and "transparency" that reality should have possessed peel away. What remains is something raw, yet with low resolution. I thought that this might be the true nature of what we truly "see."  The same goes for memories. Perhaps it's a virtual reality world tailored to our own convenience.
